clue.text: Rogue wearing a shortened garment — twice all is revealed by this!

indicators.note: a garment wearer has it around them, so the rogue sits inside the doubled letters
twice asks for the 'a' plus garment pair to be written two times over
shortened means the garment's name is cut down to its familiar short form

parts.note: a brassiere is an undergarment
a cad is an old word for a dishonourable rogue

explanation.surface: A scoundrel in skimpy underwear, with a hint of a striptease revealing everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts BRASSIERE to its everyday short form, and 'twice' means the A-plus-garment pair appears on both sides of the rogue it is wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Magicians say this incantation at the moment a trick's hidden object is shown to the audience.

clue.text: Made reference in dull read, unopened unfortunately

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters are put into a different order
a word left unopened loses its first letter, here from the word read

explanation.surface: Someone mentioned a dull book they never even opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the R of READ, leaving EAD; 'unfortunately' scrambles DULL + EAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to hint at or mention something in passing, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Maybe write new part of speech to create sonic effect

parts.note: to write something new you might rewrite it, using the prefix re- meaning again
a verb is one of the parts of speech in grammar

explanation.surface: A writer drafts a fresh section of a speech to make a bigger impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is the echoing acoustic effect added to recorded sound.

clue.text: Too easy to pick up tab after cheat promises to pay

indicators.note: after places the tab piece behind the cheat piece in the answer

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
a tab is a small label, as is a tag
an IOU ('I owe you') is a written promise to pay, plural IOUs

explanation.surface: A bill run up by a swindler who pays only in IOUs is far too easy to rack up.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease you can catch all too readily from another person is described as catching or infectious.

clue.text: Exercise, weed!

parts.note: split in two, the answer reads as an instruction to take a school physical training lesson

explanation.surface: A coach barks at a feeble pupil to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as DO PE, the answer is an order to do physical education, the school exercise lesson, so it is the wordplay that 'Exercise' paraphrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for cannabis, which is also called weed.

clue.text: Parts of bay perhaps needing to accommodate or put up local communities

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree, and boughs are parts of a tree

indicators.note: in a down answer, put up means the letters are written upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Coastal towns along a bay must house people or build upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' is not the coast but the laurel tree. In a down answer 'put up' means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town or district with its own local government.

clue.text: In pieces, seeing a northern city giving land away

indicators.note: giving with the later away means handing something over, so a word is removed from the city's name
away completes giving away, the sign that a word is removed from the city's name

parts.note: Sunderland is a city in north-east England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern city being carved up as it surrenders territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving away' removes LAND from SUNDERLAND, a city in north-east England, leaving SUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn asunder means split apart, broken into separate parts.

clue.text: Surrounded by revolutionary plain evil ne'er-do-wells — fire!

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things round, so the found letters are read backwards
the letters wanted are enclosed by the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cry to open fire on a band of revolutionary scoundrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded by' finds NEVILNE inside 'plain evil ne'er', and 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to rouse and animate them, the sense of livening up.

clue.text: Splitting the difference in ninety-nine quid is tantalising

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A price of ninety-nine pounds is tempting because it is just shy of a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A point the same distance from both ends sits halfway, like a compromise between two positions.

clue.text: Occasionally in bar, punter weeps over trouble

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the picked letters are read backwards
only now and then, so every other letter of the words is used

explanation.surface: A gambler in a pub cries over his losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes the odd letters of 'bar punter weeps', BRUTREP, and 'over' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to worry or unsettle them, as to trouble does.

clue.text: Store animal food, bagging nothing, covering rest for twenty-four hours

parts.note: to bank something is to store it for later

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so the food piece holds the others

parts.note: hay is dried grass fed to livestock
O looks like zero, nothing
a lid is a covering for a container

explanation.surface: A farmer stocks up on fodder and covers it over, taking a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' signals the insertion into the food. In Britain a bank holiday is a public holiday, when the banks once closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank holiday is a public day off work, one whole day of leisure.

clue.text: Deployed lunar dye to show what's beneath the surface?

indicators.note: deployed means set out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spreading moon-coloured dye to reveal what lies under the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlay is the padding laid beneath a carpet, literally below the floor covering.

clue.text: Massage back then study weight

indicators.note: back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: to massage is to rub
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: A back rub followed by an evening of revising heavy subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the part of the body being massaged, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is a heavy load carried, so a weight in either sense.

clue.text: Person who analyses western music packaging

parts.note: a shrink is slang for a psychoanalyst
rap is a genre of music

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst listens to cowboy music.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink-wrap is plastic film heated to fit tightly around goods as a protective cover.

clue.text: Oxygen needed by relative that runs all round the room

definitions.text: that runs all round the room

indicators.note: the oxygen is needed by, so attached after, the relative

parts.note: a dad is a father, a relative
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A family member in need of oxygen while running laps of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of an interior wall, often marked by a rail around the whole room.

clue.text: Ritualistic chapel in Snowdonia?

definitions.meaning: the ... wing of Anglicanism favours elaborate ritual
a place of worship among the Welsh mountains of Snowdonia would be a church high up

explanation.surface: A ceremonial chapel up in the mountains of North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: High Church Anglicans stress ceremony, vestments and sacraments, much like Catholic practice.

clue.text: A male duck nibbling crest of milkweed that goes up like a mushroom

definitions.text: that goes up like a mushroom

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat

indicators.note: a mouth nibbling holds a bit, so the duck piece goes around the crest

parts.note: to duck is to bob down quickly

indicators.note: the crest is the top, so the first letter of milkweed is used

explanation.surface: A drake pecking at the top of a milkweed plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird but means BOB, to dip; 'nibbling' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic bomb explosion throws up a mushroom-shaped cloud.

clue.text: EU chemists misrepresented in noted publication

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters come out in another order

explanation.surface: European chemists complain that a published paper got their findings wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed music is written in notes, so it is a publication full of notes.

clue.text: Catch up in Baltimore somehow, not at Mobile

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters are rearranged, with those of 'at' left out

explanation.surface: Someone gets caught up in Baltimore one way or another, rather than in Mobile, Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like the Alabama city but signals the anagram; 'not' removes AT from BALTIMORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to involve or entangle them in a conflict.

clue.text: Mere idiot that's loud should be quiet

indicators.note: should be says one letter must be replaced by another

parts.note: a fool is an idiot
F (forte) is the musical abbreviation for loud
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A complaint that a mere fool who is noisy ought to shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like an adjective meaning only, but it is the noun for a small lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a small lake or pond, an expanse of standing water.

clue.text: Entertaining tango, too, with no smoke and mirrors

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: overly means excessively, too
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tango show that is entertaining with no stage illusions.
explanation.definitionFit: Done openly and plainly, without deception or trickery.

clue.text: Fashionably dressed and ready to roll

definitions.meaning: wearing the trendy gear, ... being dressed in fashionable clothes
engaged and ready to move off

explanation.definitionFit: Gear means both clothing and a vehicle's engaged transmission.

clue.text: Collections of plastic measurably needing year to melt away

indicators.note: plastic means easily moulded, so the letters are reshaped, with those of year melting away

explanation.surface: Plastic records gradually warping with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like the material of records but signals the anagram; 'to melt away' removes YEAR from MEASURABLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Albums are books or records holding a gathered set of photos, stamps or songs.

clue.text: Young rebel that's got little coverage

definitions.meaning: ... were a youth subculture of rebellious shaven-headed young people
a shaven head has very little hair covering it

explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead is a youth with a closely shaved scalp, part of a rebellious subculture.

clue.text: Dandy comic second to Buster? No no!

indicators.note: No means without, so the following no is removed from the comic

parts.note: The Beano is a long-running British children's comic

indicators.note: second to means the second letter of the word buster

explanation.surface: Is The Dandy second only to Buster among comics? Certainly not!
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy, The Beano and Buster are all British children's comics. 'No' removes NO from BEANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a fashionable man, a meaning beau also carries.

clue.text: Folk riding tandem, say, more or less following anything from behind

indicators.note: following puts the more or less piece after the other
read from behind means read from the end back to the start

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything
some means approximately, as in some twenty people

explanation.surface: Cyclists on a tandem, the one behind trailing more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from behind' turns OWT, Yorkshire dialect for anything, into TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people together, such as the two riders of a bicycle built for two.

clue.text: Concerned with toffs missing grand arrival from stars?

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: missing means one letter is left out of the toffs piece

parts.note: the gentry are the upper classes, toffs
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A story about posh folk who failed to show up for a celebrity's grand entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft coming back from space into the atmosphere makes a return to Earth.

clue.text: Using childbirth, do they seek political gain?

parts.note: labour is the process of childbirth
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Asking whether people exploit having babies for political advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like part of the question but is the noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party is a British political party whose members seek power and influence.
